title: Disc stack

reference.source: Reference 9: dithered screen print of a stacked disc spring, 736 × 1282 px JPEG
reference.note: held locally; this page carries statistics measured from it and none of its pixels

summary: A domed spool and a stack of lit discs seen from above, screened by one random dither, between two flanks where one warped stripe phase prints through three light plates that slip apart where the warp bends hardest.
units: reference pixels; the plate is 736 × 1282 and every length scales with the canvas

sway.does: How far the shape moves the discs: a helix sways their centers, a resonance swells and narrows them.

turns.does: Helix turns down the stack, or half the standing-wave modes of a resonance.

rings.does: Number of discs in the stack.

spacing.does: Gap between the first two discs; lower gaps grow with the view setting.

view.does: How far above the stack the eye sits: lower discs tilt toward it and spread apart. 0 shows every disc at the same tilt.

discW.does: Long axis of each disc as a share of the sheet width. 0.4 is 145 px of half axis, as measured.

discH.does: Short axis of the top disc over its long axis.

rim.does: Thickness of each disc's lit wall: 11 px on the top disc, 23 px lower down, as measured.

inner.does: Where the lit rim ring on each disc's top face begins.

backRim.does: Width of the lit lip at the back of each disc, as a share of its width at the front.

lip.does: Speck coverage of each disc's lit lip; 1.01 prints it solid, lower lets the screen pit it as the reference's lips are.

streaky.does: How much the gray on each disc face streaks along the ellipse. 0.4 is the measured scan.

face.does: Speck coverage inside each disc's top face, under the ridges.

halo.does: Speck ramp the lit edges bleed into the dark: 0.4 is 2.4 px.

base.does: The last disc is wider by 15 % at 1, a foot for the stack.

column.does: Width of the domed gray spool behind the discs: 216 px measured just under each disc.

gray.does: Speck coverage of the spool: the tone the dither screens.

sheen.does: How much brighter the spool prints near its edges, where the turned surface catches side light.

even.does: How much of the spool and disc screen is an even blue-noise threshold instead of a random one. 0 is the measured static.

grain.does: Cell size of the dither grid; above 1 px each speck gets a soft ramp.

speckVar.does: Spread of brightness between specks: each speck prints at 1 minus up to this much, so a fine screen still carries a spread of grays.

tooth.does: Slow noise added to the tone before the threshold, strongest at mid-gray and nil at black and white; clumps the specks without pitting a lit lip.

dust.does: Stray half-tone specks on the unprinted black.

chainTone.does: Share of each hairline that prints: the lines print in 5 px dashes, and 1 prints them solid.

chainPitch.does: Spacing of the hairlines beside the stripes: 5 to 6 px by autocorrelation; the sparse lines outside the stripes sit 1.7 times wider.

chainW.does: Width of the hairline band between the black gap and the stripes; the lines thicken toward the stripes.

gapW.does: Unprinted black between the disc edge and the first chain line.

stripes.does: Width of the stripe zone where no bulge flares it.

pitch.does: Line spacing of the stripe screen: 11 px by autocorrelation.

flare.does: Strength of the three bulges per flank where the stripe zone flares outward and the lines go bold.

reach.does: How far a bulge pushes the stripe zone toward the edge.

fan.does: How much the lines spread apart inside a bulge: a displacement that grows against the distance from the inner edge, so the pitch opens outward.

warp.does: Sideways wave of the sheet that bends every stripe.

lineSoft.does: Blur of the light plates: the stripe edges of the reference ramp over about 2 px.

print.does: Half width of the band, wandering down each flank, where the stripes print bold through the light plates; a bulge widens it. Outside it the same lines stay dashed hairlines.

dash.does: Length of the dashes each hairline breaks into.

weight.does: Share of each stripe period the green plate prints; the bulges and the beat add to it.

fold.does: Strength of the eye in each bulge: a gaussian push on the stripe phase; above about 0.6 the lines fold into closed loops.

murk.does: Dim specks the screen leaves across the black flanks; the reference's flank black is 7 % dark gray specks.

haze.does: Share of the flank black carrying a dim speck, 4 to 30 % gray: the reference's black has a third of its pixels in the lowest gray bins.

beat.does: A straight screen this many lines per cycle finer beats against the warped one and sets the line weight: the moire.

misreg.does: Sideways slip of the red and blue plates off the green, in space; it doubles inside the bulges. A fold, where the lines run flat, shows no fringe.

phase.does: Position along the loop. Turns the helix once round the spool (a resonance swells and narrows once), runs the sheet warp down the flanks one full wave and slides the hairline dashes down 37.5 px.

seed.does: Re-rolls the dither, the bulges and the edge strip.

modes.saw: value up to value + amp over period seconds, then again
modes.drift: seeded walk, one step of up to amp every period seconds, folded back at the slider ends

motion.runs: only while Motion is on, at half scale; the sliders hold the center values; off by default

live.runs: only while Live is on: a drag on the figure sets x across and y down between these ends; off by default

techniques.name: Edge
techniques.implementation: The top disc's wall: solid white, 11 px tall, the lip above it narrows to a quarter of its width at the back.

techniques.name: Grain
techniques.implementation: Inside a disc face: thin ridges under the lit lip, then the spool's speckle at 47 % coverage.

techniques.name: Pull
techniques.implementation: The bold band: yellow where the red plate sits on the green, a thin red edge on one side and the black between.

pass_order: the stack: 11 discs from 16 % of the height down, each placed by the eye's height above it, so lower discs sit further apart and tilt further toward the eye; each disc is a top face, a lit lip and a wall
the spool: a domed gray column behind the discs, brighter toward its edges

the flanks: a black gap, a band of 1 px hairlines in dashes, then one warped stripe phase; the warp is a sum of two sines whose depth grows inside three bulges per flank, each carrying an eye that folds the lines
the bold band: a band that wanders down each flank, widened by the bulges, where the stripes print through the light plates; outside it the same lines stay dashed hairlines

the light plates: green on the line, red a little narrower and slipped one way, blue narrower still and slipped the other way, only inside the bulges; the slip is in space, so a steep run of lines fringes and a fold does not
the edge strip: a lit band 12 px wide that runs cyan to yellow-green down the sheet, a dim blue rule inside it
the screen: one hashed threshold per 1.35 px cell turns every gray into speck density; each speck takes a little of its own brightness; a 0.5 px press blur
flank haze: dim 1 px specks over the black, the scanned sheet's own gray

measured.ring_method: peaks of the 80 px wide center column luminance, smoothed over 9 rows
measured.disc_axis_method: first and last x above 185 in the 45 rows over each ring row

front_band_rows_px.method: rows above 180 through the center column at each ring

measured.spool_method: speckle coverage above 110 in rows 14 to 24 px under each disc
measured.hairline_evidence: column-mean autocorrelation of x 176 to 200 peaks at lags 5 and 6

stripe_kmeans_10.method: k-means on every third pixel of x 60 to 180, y 300 to 1000

measured.rejected: a dotted outline for each ring (the first build): the reference's rims measure 11 to 25 px of solid white

benchmark.computed: live, when this page loads, by the code that measured the reference: default parameters, Screen print palette, 1× reference size

setup.note: Every rect compares in place. The plate places 11 discs within 6 px of the reference's ring rows, so the spool, disc front and disc face rects sit on the same events; the hairline, stripe and edge rects sit on the same zones of the flanks, whose bulges are the plate's own. Composition moved from the first build (9 discs, 7 different rects), so all rects were re-picked against the new stack; search.py on the spool and disc rects found nothing better than the in-place windows.

limits: Benchmark mean 0.931, lowest 0.66 (edge strip yellow-green color). Under 98 % on: the hairline band (tone histogram 0.80, mean 0.79): the reference's hairlines are scanned 1 px lines whose gray spreads over bins 1 to 8, the plate's are 1 px dashes at one gray each, so it prints too much pure black; the stripes' autocorrelation (0.72) and yellow (0.83): the reference's lines are near vertical with a 22 px repeat that survives its warp, the plate's bold band folds harder and wanders more, which reads better next to the reference but decorrelates faster; the edge strip's yellow-green (0.66), whose reference band is a saturated (169,215,53) the additive plates reach only at full print.
Render time 0.86 to 1.3 s on this machine depending on load; the two Catmull-Rom upsamples and five blurs take about a third of it.

The stack and the flanks are the plate's own: 11 discs placed by a view height, three bulges per flank from the seed; the ring rows land within 6 px of the reference's, the bulges do not sit where its flares do.
The reference is a JPEG; its ringing around the stripes is not modeled.
notes: Deterministic: the same palette, parameters and seed give the same pixels.
A display render is capped at 2.4 megapixels; a slider in motion draws at half scale (down to a quarter on a heavy engine) and the release redraws in full.
This spec follows the controls: open it again, or leave it open, after changing them.
